name: step_entry_counter_spawn_enemy
description: Increments a per-entry counter and, when a specific mode value and a free enemy slot line up, fills that slot's position and sprite fields and claims it. In its other branch it either draws the entry or clears it, and it also steps through a short state sequence that can trigger a sound.

name: draw_masked_rows_three_planes
description: Loops over a few rows and, for each one, ORs masked bit patterns read from a table into three bit-plane buffers at a computed screen offset. It exits early once the computed screen coordinate goes past the visible limit.

name: update_and_plot_starfield
description: Walks forty star slots, moving each one by a scroll delta and respawning it from a running counter when it expires or leaves the visible range. Visible stars are plotted by XOR-ing single pixels into three bit-planes, with a faster speed when the space flag is set.

name: draw_life_icon_blit
description: Waits for the blitter to go idle, then if the lives count is below six it programs a blitter copy with masks and pointers, taking the source from a table indexed by the play-off value and the lives count.

name: blit_smart_counter_icon
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle and returns if the smart-bomb count is above five. Otherwise it programs a blitter copy whose source comes from a table indexed by the play-off value and the smart count.

name: erase_life_icon_blit
description: When the lives count is between one and five, waits for the blitter twice, programs a blitter operation with masks and pointers, and sets the size register to start the transfer. The source pointer is chosen from a table indexed by the play-off value and the lives count.

name: erase_smart_icon_blit
description: When the smart-bomb count is between one and five, waits for the blitter to be idle, programs its control, mask and pointer registers, then starts a blit whose source comes from a table indexed by the play-off value and the smart count.

name: redraw_score_by_magnitude
description: Calls the same redraw routine once for each score threshold the score has passed, and again when the score differs from its saved backup copy. Its other compare is a self-comparison with no effect.

name: draw_score_digit_pair_rows
description: Copies eight rows of glyph bytes from a table into two bit-plane buffers for a pair of digit values, writing the second digit only when a flag byte is zero. A digit value of zero is replaced by the index ten before the lookup.

name: dispatch_copper_and_vblank_irqs
description: Reads the interrupt request and enable registers, ANDs them together, and calls the copper interrupt handler when its bit is set. It then calls the vertical blank handler if that bit is set.

name: signal_vblank_flag
description: Sets the global flag word to 32 to mark that a vertical blank has happened.

name: run_per_frame_game_update
description: Runs once per frame when the frame-done flag is set: it switches screens, applies the scroll value and cycles an animation counter, then draws icons. Unless the game is stopped it also runs shot and bomb updates, the star field, the hyperspace and smart timers, and the ship and enemy logic, spawning an enemy entry when the level timer runs out.

name: read_keyboard_serial_code
description: Reads a keyboard byte from the serial data register when a flag is set, decodes the key number and its press or release bit, and records it in the last-key variable and the key state table. It then waits for the handshake flag and clears it.

name: acknowledge_keyboard_handshake
description: Clears the last-key variable and one key-state byte, then waits for the keyboard handshake flag and sets the handshake value to acknowledge it. It is reached as a branch from the keyboard reader.

name: update_enemy_slots_and_waves
description: Walks the enemy slot table each frame, moving active entries and running their per-type state changes, sound triggers and shot or bomb hooks. When the level's enemy list is exhausted it clears the slots, halts the game for a wave pause, adds a life and refreshes the life icons, and when a pending award flag is set it adds a life and a smart count.

name: add_bcd_score_award_check
description: Adds an amount to the score held as packed decimal digits, applying decimal correction to each byte. It sets a pending extra-life flag when the upper digit of the score changes.

name: launch_bomb_from_free_slot
description: When a bomb slot is free, the frame parity matches and the source is within a horizontal window of the map position, it writes the bomb's horizontal position and a start height into that slot. It then sets the slot's timer and marks the slot as used.

name: update_bombs_and_ship_hits
description: Walks the bomb slots each frame, counting down each bomb's timer and freeing expired ones. Bombs in the visible window are drawn into three bit-planes, and when one lies in the ship's vertical and horizontal collision zone the game is flagged to stop with reason code two.

name: fire_shot_into_free_slot
description: If a shot slot is free and the target lies within the visible window, it plays a shot sound, writes the shot's position and then a velocity derived from the ship's speed and facing. Finally it clears the free-slot index so the slot is taken.

name: update_and_draw_shots
description: Walks the shot slots, advancing each shot by its velocity and freeing it when it leaves the visible range or hits the top or bottom edge. Live shots are drawn into the bit-planes, and a shot that overlaps the ship's collision zone stops the game with reason code two.

name: flip_double_buffer_planes
description: Toggles between two screen buffers: it saves the current plane pointers, loads the other buffer's pointer values, and points the active planes at it. It then calls the clear routine on the newly selected buffer.

name: blit_clear_screen_plane
description: Waits for the blitter to go idle, then programs it with full-screen size and masks and no source channel, writing to the buffer named by the first plane pointer. It then starts the blit.

name: initialise_system_and_video
description: Runs the start-up sequence in order: saves the system registers, shuts down the operating system, installs the vertical blank handler, sets up interrupts, sets the initial screen pointers and builds the copper list.

name: set_initial_screen_pointers
description: Stores fixed low and high word values into three plane pointer variables and three alternate pointer variables, setting the starting screen buffer addresses. It takes no inputs and returns nothing.

name: install_vblank_handler
description: Stores the address of the new vertical blank handler in a global variable and writes an interrupt-enable value that turns on the master interrupt bit along with the vertical blank, copper and ports bits.

name: setup_keyboard_timer_interrupt
description: Stores the address of the keyboard handler, then writes interrupt and timer register values for the first CIA chip. It finishes by clearing one bit in a control byte.

name: shut_down_and_restore_system
description: Disables interrupts and DMA by calling the system kill routine, then calls the revive routine to put the saved system state back. It returns nothing.

name: save_graphics_and_hardware_state
description: Opens the graphics library and saves the current view and copper list pointers. It also saves the interrupt enable and DMA control register values and makes one graphics library call.

name: disable_interrupts_and_dma
description: Writes a value with every bit set except the enable flag to the DMA control and interrupt enable registers, turning off all DMA channels and interrupts.

name: restore_saved_hardware_state
description: Disables everything, then restores the saved copper pointer, vertical blank and level-two interrupt vectors, and the saved DMA and interrupt enable values with the enable flag set. It waits for a status bit, makes one graphics library call and closes the graphics library.

name: open_graphics_library_retry
description: Repeatedly calls the library-open routine through a stored pointer until it returns a non-zero base address, then keeps that address in a global variable.

name: open_dos_library_retry
description: Repeatedly calls the library-open routine through a stored pointer until it returns a non-zero base address, then keeps that address for the DOS library in a global variable.

name: start_program_parse_arguments
description: Program entry point: it opens the DOS library, allocates a state record, and splits the command-line text into words. Quoted words use asterisk escapes for newline and escape characters, and the NIL: device is referenced, then the main pager runs and resources are freed.

name: release_program_resources
description: Stores its argument in the program state record, then conditionally closes a file handle, replies to a message port, frees a memory block and closes a library, each guarded by a stored pointer. It returns the saved argument.

name: run_file_pager_loop
description: Main pager routine: it sets up the display window and opens the named file, showing a percentage progress prompt and a quit hint. It then loops reading input until the file ends or the user quits, and reports 'Can't open window' and 'End of File' messages from its text.

name: call_four_table_entries
description: Calls a routine four times, once per entry of a four-slot global table, passing each entry together with a value taken from the structure it receives.

name: check_buffer_bytes_allowed
description: Makes two library calls on a handle with an 80-byte buffer, then scans that buffer and returns one when every byte falls in the accepted character ranges, and zero otherwise.

name: dispatch_pager_key_command
description: Waits for a key with a timeout, skips escape sequences, and dispatches the key code through a large switch. Among the branches it starts a line search for one key and handles several navigation keys, returning a status value to its caller.

name: run_pager_navigation_action
description: Calls a few library routines with the pager state and then runs a stored routine through a pointer. Its text covers reopening the file, launching the editor named in the environment, finding the previous page and showing the help hint.

name: initialise_page_and_loop
description: Sets the line counter to one and the stop flag to zero, calls a file routine and stores its result. It then repeatedly calls the paging routine while more lines remain and the stop flag is still clear.

name: read_chunk_and_count_lines
description: Reads a block into the line buffer through two library calls and stores the byte count. When the first flag is zero it also increments the page line counter.

name: read_next_text_line
description: Reads up to 128 bytes into the buffer and scans forward to the next newline or form-feed, returning how many characters that line holds. A form-feed is rewritten as a visible caret-L marker and sets a flag.

name: display_page_until_full
description: Works out how many lines fit on a page from a few flags, then prints lines from the line table until the page is full or the file ends. It then reads a key and stops when that key is the quit key or control-C.

name: search_text_across_pages
description: Shows a searching message, then repeatedly reads a block and scans it for the search string until a match is found or the file ends. It returns one on a match and zero when no match is found.

name: run_pager_call_with_setup
description: Runs a fixed sequence around one main call: it prepares the state record, optionally writes a buffer, calls the supplied routine with the parameter, then releases the state. It returns the result of the main call.

name: call_and_conditionally_flush
description: Calls a routine with two arguments, then calls a second routine with the first argument only when a flag in the state record is zero.

name: update_page_position_display
description: Calls the output routine with the file handle and a stored value, then calls it again with the stored line limit from the state record.

name: redraw_bottom_line_row
description: Calls the output routine with a zero offset and a count of one, then calls it again with the stored line limit minus one.

name: draw_text_rows_wrapped
description: Draws up to the requested number of rows from the text buffer, writing at most 128 characters per chunk and counting line breaks. It stops early when a form-feed sets the stop flag, then writes a final newline.

name: call_chain_then_handler
description: Calls a routine with its argument, then calls a second routine through a function pointer kept in the state record, passing the global table as its data.

name: set_page_flag_and_forward
description: When a field in the state record is zero, sets a short field in a linked record to one. It then calls a routine with the global table as its data.

name: call_output_with_flag_args
description: Calls an output routine with one of two argument sets chosen by a flag in the state record: zeros, or a count made from the stored line limit plus one.

name: print_prompt_by_flag
description: Calls an output routine with the file handle and either three copies of the global table pointer or the stored line limit, depending on a flag. Its text reference is a two-string format.

name: seek_and_return_clamped_position
description: Makes two seek calls with a zero offset, then returns the second result, clamped to zero when it is negative.

name: copy_chunk_from_read_buffer
description: Takes up to the requested number of bytes from the read buffer in the state record, refilling it first when it runs short. It copies them to the destination through a library call, advances the buffer offsets, and returns the number of bytes copied.

name: refill_read_buffer_block
description: Flushes a pending full buffer block if one exists, then reads up to 4096 bytes into the read buffer through a library call. It updates the remaining byte count and the buffer offsets from what was read.

name: update_scroll_window_position
description: Works out a target line from the base, start or end position chosen by a mode argument, then checks it against the current window bounds. Inside the bounds it updates the window offsets, and outside them it moves the window and redraws through a display routine.

name: read_line_from_buffer
description: Reads characters one at a time through a source call into the destination until a newline or 127 characters are read. It then adds a terminator and returns the count read.

name: copy_null_terminated_string
description: Copies bytes from a source string to a destination one at a time, including the terminating zero byte.

name: convert_string_to_uppercase
description: Walks a null-terminated string and changes each letter from a to z into its capital by subtracting the case offset. Other characters are left unchanged.

name: parse_signed_decimal
description: Reads an optional plus or minus sign, then accumulates decimal digits from the string into an integer. The result is negated when the sign was minus.

name: call_library_with_full_mask
description: When both the value and the stored pointer are non-null, calls a library routine with the stored pointer, the value and an all-ones mask. Otherwise it does nothing.

name: finish_and_free_request
description: Writes its text argument to the output when it is not empty, waits for a newline if a flag is set, then frees and restores the linked buffers and fields of the request record. It ends with the final cleanup call.

name: send_single_byte_message
description: Stores its argument in a one-element stack buffer and passes it to a library call as a one-byte message. It returns that call's result.

name: copy_record_fields_then_free
description: Allocates a 36-byte record through a library call and, if that succeeds, reads a value from the stored port into a small stack buffer. It copies two fields from the record into the caller's structure, then frees the record.

name: allocate_linked_record_copy
description: Allocates a 68-byte record and links it into a list through library calls, then copies a given number of words from the source array into it. It returns the record's stored field, or zero when the allocation or lookup fails.

name: forward_with_stack_pointer
description: Forwards its two arguments to a second routine together with a pointer to a fixed stack slot.

name: read_single_byte_or_fail
description: Calls a routine to fill a one-byte stack buffer. It returns that byte as a signed value when the call reports exactly one byte, and minus one otherwise.

name: format_message_and_emit
description: Formats text into a 140-byte stack buffer through a library formatting call, measures its length, and passes the text and length to a second routine when it is not empty.

name: divide_32bit_with_remainder
description: Divides a 32-bit value by a 16-bit divisor. It uses repeated shift-and-subtract when the divisor is large, and two 16-bit divisions otherwise, returning the quotient and remainder.

name: multiply_32bit_partial_products
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values using 16-bit partial products and returns the 32-bit product.

name: stub_self_call_recursion
description: Only calls itself and returns, so it does no real work and is best treated as a stub or decoded padding.

name: negate_result_if_flagged
description: Calls a routine and returns its first result, negated when the second return register is non-zero.

name: call_library_entry_from_table
description: Calls a library routine through a function pointer stored at a fixed offset in the global table, then returns.

name: store_byte_at_pointer
description: Stores the low byte of the data register at the address held in the pointer register, then returns. It works as the per-character output callback for a formatting call.

name: allocate_and_send_message
description: Allocates a 34-byte message block through a library call and fills in its fields from the arguments and a value from another library call. It dispatches the block to one of two targets depending on the first argument, and returns the block or zero when no port or allocation is available.

name: release_message_port_block
description: When a field in the block is non-zero it first calls a removal routine. It then marks the block as deleted, clears its signal field, releases the signal bit and frees the block through a library call.

name: search_substring_before_newline
description: Searches the first string for the second one, stopping at a newline. It returns one when the second string occurs within it and zero otherwise, including when the second string is empty.

name: initialise_list_header_node
description: Sets the first word of a block to point four bytes past its own start, clears the second word, and points the third word back at the block.

name: copy_table_block_and_call
description: When the destination pointer on the stack is non-null, copies sixteen 32-bit words from a fixed table in the data area into it. It then calls the routine held in a pointer register.

name: launch_command_in_new_process
description: Program entry: scans a list for the largest size value, then builds a 140-byte buffer and a new process block. It sets the process entry point to a local routine and returns zero when the process starts, or minus one on failure.

name: copy_startup_block_and_call
description: When the destination pointer on the stack is non-null, copies sixteen 32-bit words from a fixed table into it. It then calls the routine held in a pointer register.

name: launch_command_in_new_process
description: Program entry: scans a list for the largest size value, then builds a 140-byte buffer and a new process block. It sets the process entry point to a local routine and returns zero when the process starts, or minus one on failure.

name: copy_startup_block_and_call
description: When the destination pointer on the stack is non-null, copies sixteen 32-bit words from a fixed table into it. It then calls the routine held in a pointer register.

name: start_program_parse_arguments
description: Program entry point: it opens the DOS library, allocates a state record, and splits the command-line text into words. Quoted words use asterisk escapes for newline and escape characters, and the NIL: device is referenced, then the main routine runs and resources are freed.

name: release_program_resources
description: Stores its argument in the program state record, then conditionally closes a file handle, replies to a message port, frees a memory block and closes a library, each guarded by a stored pointer. It returns the saved argument.

name: start_workbench_tool_task
description: Looks up a resident tag for the named tool and starts it as a task inside a forbid and permit pair. It reports 'Cannot find resident tag' or 'Cannot start tool' with an error number when a step fails. A string is passed through the same XOR pass twice, which leaves it unchanged.

name: compare_strings_ordered
description: Compares two null-terminated strings and returns minus one when the first is less than the second, one when it is greater, and zero when they are equal.

name: build_linked_list_from_table
description: Walks a table of entries, allocating an 8-byte node for each one and copying in a value obtained through a library call. The nodes are linked into a new list and its head is returned.

name: call_library_vector_132
description: Calls a library function at a fixed negative offset from the library base held in a global variable, then returns.

name: call_library_vector_138
description: Calls a library function at a fixed negative offset from the library base held in a global variable, then returns.

name: call_library_vector_198
description: Calls a library function at a fixed negative offset from the library base held in a global variable, then returns.

name: call_library_vector_294
description: Calls a library function at a fixed negative offset from the library base held in a global variable, then returns.

name: call_library_vector_366
description: Calls a library function at a fixed negative offset from the library base held in a global variable, then returns.

name: call_library_vector_372
description: Calls a library function at a fixed negative offset from the library base held in a global variable, then returns.

name: call_library_vector_384
description: Calls a library function at a fixed negative offset from the library base held in a global variable, then returns.

name: call_library_vector_414
description: Calls a library function at a fixed negative offset from the library base held in a global variable, then returns.

name: call_library_vector_552
description: Calls a library function at a fixed negative offset from the library base held in a global variable, then returns.

name: call_library_vector_624
description: Calls a library function at a fixed negative offset from the library base held in a global variable, then returns.

name: check_release_name_suffix
description: Compares the start of a name with a reference string, and when the version character equals '2' it rewrites the short suffix after it with a dot and spaces. Its text reference is a Workbench release string, and it stops early on a mismatch.

name: write_dot_padding_suffix
description: Writes a dot followed by four spaces into five consecutive bytes of the buffer at a fixed offset.

name: match_reference_prefix
description: Advances through the buffer while its bytes match the reference string, stopping at the end of the reference or at the first mismatch.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Performs no operations and returns immediately, so it is an empty routine called from other places.

name: reschedule_current_task
description: Calls the operating system's reschedule function through the exec library base and returns. It takes no inputs and returns nothing.

name: dispatch_task_scheduler
description: Calls the operating system's dispatch function through the exec library base and returns. It takes no inputs and returns nothing.

name: allocate_memory_block
description: Calls the operating system's memory allocation function through the exec library base and returns. It takes no inputs and returns nothing.

name: forward_with_stack_pointer
description: Forwards its two arguments to a second routine together with a pointer to a fixed stack slot, then returns.

name: format_message_and_emit
description: Formats text into a 140-byte stack buffer through a library formatting call, measures its length, and passes the text and length to a second routine when it is not empty.

name: store_byte_at_pointer
description: Stores the low byte of the data register at the address held in the pointer register, then returns. It works as the per-character output callback for a formatting call.

name: copy_block_then_jump_target
description: Program entry: copies a block of memory through the exec library's copy routine, then makes an indirect call to a jump target that the decompiler could not resolve. The target is not identified in the evidence.

name: create_ramdrive_unit
description: Opens the exec and DOS libraries, locates the device structure and sets up a new unit. It allocates a memory block for the disk image, writes a DOS type tag, fills a 128-entry table and stores a checksum of that table.

name: create_ramdrive_unit_from_params
description: Copies a parameter block from the request into the global buffer, then sets up a unit the same way as the main routine. It allocates the image memory, writes the DOS type tag, fills a 128-entry table and stores its checksum.

name: copy_params_and_init_unit
description: Copies a block of bytes from the source to the destination, then sets up a unit in the same way as the other setup routines. It returns zero.

name: initialize_ramdrive_device
description: Stores pointers to the device's internal buffers and control fields and links the device into a global list. It then fills a 128-entry table with a pattern from a global variable, sets extra fields from a global flag, and stores a checksum of the table.

name: call_library_vector_210
description: Calls a library function at a fixed negative offset twice in a row, then returns zero.

name: find_fitting_memory_node
description: Disables interrupts with a nesting count, then walks a linked list of memory nodes for one whose attribute flags include the requested mask and whose size is large enough. It records the size of a fitting node and calls a library routine with the result, returning that result.

name: find_fitting_node_and_allocate
description: Walks a linked list of memory nodes whose attribute flags include the requested mask, recording a size that fits the request. When the count argument is non-zero it calls a library allocation routine and returns its result, otherwise it returns zero.

name: decrement_interrupt_nesting
description: Decrements the interrupt-disable nesting count and re-enables interrupts when the count was already at its lowest level. It returns zero.

name: store_field_and_return_zero
description: Stores the data-register value into a fixed field of the structure in the address register, then returns zero.

name: dispatch_device_request
description: Forbids task switching, then dispatches the request to a handler picked from a 16-entry table by its command number and stores the result back in the request. It replies to the request when a flag is clear, and finishes by permitting task switching and calling the cleanup routine.

name: return_minus_three_error
description: Returns the constant minus three as an error code without doing any other work.

name: remove_unit_and_free_memory
description: Decrements the unit's use count and, when it drops below zero and the unit is still linked, unlinks it from the device list and the global list. It then frees the unit's memory block and appends a colon to its name.

name: unlink_unit_and_append_colon
description: Copies a stored value into the output location and removes a unit from the global list, then calls a library routine for it. It then appends a colon to the end of the name string and makes the final cleanup call.

name: copy_value_and_append_colon
description: Stores a value into the output location and calls a library routine. It then appends a colon to the end of the name string and makes a final cleanup call.

name: stub_unimplemented_halt
description: Only calls an unimplemented-halt marker, so this is a stub with no behaviour of its own in the library.

name: store_argument_in_global
description: Copies the address-register argument into a global variable slot and returns.

name: expunge_library_when_unused
description: If the library's open count is zero, unlinks it from the library list and frees its memory through a library call, then returns a saved value. Otherwise it sets the expunge-pending flag bit and returns zero.

name: set_expunge_pending_flag
description: Sets the expunge-pending flag bit in the library structure and returns zero.

name: open_and_count_library_use
description: Unless the library is marked for expunge, increments its open count and, on the first open, loads the companion mathffp.library through a library routine. It returns the library base, or minus one when the library is marked for expunge.

name: return_failure_minus_one
description: Returns minus one, the library's failure result, and does nothing else.

name: close_and_expunge_idle_library
description: Decrements the library's open count. When the count reaches zero and the expunge-pending flag is set, it runs the expunge routine and returns its result, and when the count reaches zero it also calls a routine with a stored value. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: forward_call_no_arguments
description: Calls another routine with no arguments and returns, as a thin wrapper.

name: compute_float_mantissa_bits
description: Builds the mantissa bits of a floating-point value held in the data register through a loop of up to 23 shift-and-subtract steps. Zero returns at once, and negative inputs are handed to a separate routine.

name: divide_bits_with_rounding
description: Sets one bit in the value from an index, then runs a shift-and-subtract loop over the given number of bit steps. It rounds the result up by one in some cases, unless it is already at its maximum, and returns the adjusted value.

name: call_and_set_status_bits
description: Calls a library routine, then clears bit 3 and sets bit 1 in its result before returning it.

name: run_fixed_float_op_sequence
description: Calls a fixed sequence of entries through the library base at three fixed offsets, alternating between two of them and ending with a third. It takes no arguments and returns nothing.

name: run_float_op_sign_branch
description: Runs a series of floating-point primitives through library offsets, with the path chosen by comparison results and an extra step when the input is negative. It returns the final status value with bits 1 and 3 cleared.

name: run_float_op_three_branch
description: Runs floating-point primitives through library offsets along one of three paths, chosen by comparison results and the sign of the input. It returns the final status value with some status bits cleared.

name: dispatch_float_sign_zero_path
description: Checks a zero-test value and the sign of the input, then runs the matching sequence of floating-point primitives through library offsets. It returns the status with bits masked off.

name: dispatch_float_primitive_by_sign
description: Runs one of a few floating-point primitive sequences chosen by a zero test and the sign of the input, then returns the status with bits masked off.

name: dispatch_float_sign_only
description: Runs one floating-point primitive chosen by the sign of the input and a zero-test value, then returns the status with bits masked off.

name: run_float_primitive_masked_status
description: Calls one floating-point primitive through the library base, then returns the status with bits masked off.

name: run_float_primitive_pair_masked
description: Calls one floating-point primitive twice through the library base, then returns the status with bits masked off.

name: run_float_primitive_pair_masked
description: Calls one floating-point primitive twice through the library base, then returns the status with bits masked off.

name: call_library_vector_414
description: Calls a library function at a fixed negative offset from the library base held in a global variable, then returns.

name: call_library_vector_552
description: Calls a library function at a fixed negative offset from the library base held in a global variable, then returns.

name: compute_float_quotient_bits
description: Works on the exponent and mantissa bits of a floating-point value, checking for an out-of-range case first. It then runs a shift-and-subtract loop of up to 24 steps to produce the quotient bits, and calls a routine afterwards when the overflow flag is set.

name: compute_shift_subtract_quotient
description: Runs a shift-and-subtract loop of up to 24 steps over the input value to build its quotient bits. It calls a routine if the loop runs out of steps, and calls another when a flag byte is non-zero.

name: run_shift_subtract_until_exhausted
description: Runs a shift-and-subtract loop that stops when its step counter argument runs out. It calls a routine at that point, and calls another when a flag byte is non-zero.

name: compute_trig_angle_iteration
description: Reduces an angle held in the data register by repeatedly adding or subtracting a fixed constant, then runs a 23-step shift-and-add iteration over a table of constants. It produces a pair of results and passes them out through library calls.

name: compute_trig_angle_range_checked
description: Returns early for angles outside a set range, otherwise reduces the angle and runs the same 23-step iteration as its neighbours. It then passes the result out through library calls, with an extra call when the result is non-zero.

name: reduce_angle_and_accumulate
description: Reduces the angle the same way as its neighbouring routines, then accumulates table constants over 23 steps. It calls a routine to store the accumulated result.

name: compute_trig_angle_sign_check
description: Returns early for small angles, reduces the angle and runs the 23-step iteration, then takes one of several output paths based on the sign and value of a stack argument.

name: compute_trig_angle_single_output
description: Reduces the angle the same way as its neighbours, runs the 23-step iteration, then makes one output library call. Inputs outside the accepted range return early.

name: compute_trig_angle_signed_output
description: Reduces the angle, runs the 23-step iteration, and outputs through library calls. The output path is chosen by the sign of a stack argument and whether its high word equals minus one.

name: iterate_trig_constants_output
description: Runs a 23-step shift-and-add iteration whose constants come from a register, then outputs the result through library calls. The path taken depends on the sign of a stack argument.

name: run_trig_iteration_output
description: Runs the 23-step shift-and-add iteration on the input angle and outputs the result through library calls. The output path depends on the sign of a stack argument.

name: run_table_shift_loop_output
description: Runs a shift-and-add loop over a table for a count argument, then outputs the result through library calls. The output path depends on the sign of a stack argument.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Does nothing and returns, so it is an empty routine.

name: forward_call_no_arguments
description: Calls another routine with no arguments and returns, as a thin wrapper.

name: call_two_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls two routines one after the other with no arguments, then returns.

name: normalise_float_value_bits
description: Normalises a 32-bit value by shifting it left until its top bit is set, adjusting a 16-bit exponent from a fixed base. Negative inputs are negated first and the sign is handled in the exponent. Values already in range skip the shifting.

name: normalise_shifted_value_bits
description: Normalises a value held in the data register by shifting it left until its top bit is set, adjusting a 16-bit exponent from a fixed base. It returns at once when its input is zero, and handles negative values in the same way as its neighbour.

name: call_then_conditional_pair
description: Calls one routine, then calls two more in sequence when a flag stays false. The flag is fixed to false, so the two follow-up calls always run.

name: call_one_then_three_routines
description: Calls one routine, then calls three more in sequence because a fixed flag stays false.

name: call_routines_with_incremented_byte
description: When the input byte is non-zero and incrementing it does not overflow, calls one routine, then calls two routines with the incremented byte and one more routine.

name: pack_float_exponent_and_sign
description: Returns at once for a zero input. Otherwise it works out an exponent shift from the low bits of the value, rebuilds the sign and mantissa word, and calls several routines to finish the packed result.

name: call_four_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls four routines one after another with no arguments, then returns.

name: accumulate_signed_table_sum
description: Walks a table of 32-bit values for a count, adding each value when the accumulator is negative and subtracting it otherwise. It returns when the count runs out.

name: accumulate_table_until_negative
description: Adds the first table entry to an accumulator, then subtracts successive entries while the accumulator stays non-negative. It stops when the count runs out.

name: encode_float_mantissa_exponent
description: Returns early through a routine for a zero input. Otherwise it computes the mantissa with a shift-and-subtract loop and finishes with routine calls, using the sign to adjust the exponent.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Does nothing and returns, so it is an empty routine.

name: encode_float_mantissa_scaled
description: Calls two routines, then computes the mantissa with a shift-and-subtract loop of up to 22 steps. It finishes with routine calls, using the exponent byte to choose the scaling.

name: run_mantissa_loop_with_scaling
description: Runs a shift-and-subtract loop limited by a count argument, then scales the result by a biased exponent byte and calls output routines. It returns early when the exponent byte is zero.

name: call_three_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls three routines in succession, then returns.

name: round_and_pack_float_value
description: For a non-negative input it calls two routines, works out a rounding decision from the exponent bits, and packs the result with its sign through further routine calls. Negative inputs take a separate routine path.

name: pack_float_after_calls
description: Calls two routines, returns early for a zero input, then computes a shifted mantissa from the exponent bits and packs the value through routine calls, using the sign to fix up the result.
